items.reason: The moiety must use INN spelling. The record gives "Niacin CRT (other names: Nicotinic acid, Vitamin B3)", and the INN is nicotinic acid.

Nicotinic acid is a licensed medicine (the record cites its use for "the management of dyslipidaemias"), tested for antitumour effect ("Evaluating if Niacin CRT Improves Glioblastoma Survival Rates"). A licensed medicine also sold as a supplement is pharmacological (§1.2) and a candidate under D30-R5. Licensing of the specific 'Niacin CRT' product is not stated and must be documented in Table S2.
It is the only investigational agent, added to the Stupp regimen ("adding Niacin CRT™ to standard first line treatment"), so rule 4 applies. It is a candidate if licensed as a medicine (D30-R5).

note: D31 §D evidence check pending (R5 licensing, Table S2: Niacin CRT); proposal stays as drafted. The candidate status depends on D30-R5 licensing evidence for the Niacin CRT product (Canadian sponsor), to be recorded in Table S2. If that product is unlicensed and only a supplement, the trial would become excluded_intervention_type. Target engagement is yes from the planned niacin activity in peripheral innate immune cells (blood pharmacodynamics).
